summary: Mathematical dossier for A FRONTIER FOR THE ZEROS: a 220-second film with verified numerical geometry and an attributed account of the manuscript’s argument.
content:
Preserve the approved eight-act timing: 24 + 22 + 30 + 32 + 26 + 22 + 46 + 18 = 220 seconds, including transitions and reading pauses. Display the following formulas sequentially, with at most one main formula and two explanatory lines.

Write \(s=\sigma+it\). Initially, \(\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-s}=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1}\) only for \(\sigma>1\). Analytic continuation supplies the strip values; its sole singularity is the simple pole at \(s=1\), of residue one. A zero satisfies \(\zeta(\rho)=0\). Dirichlet characters are periodic multiplicative weights, zero on nonunits; \(L(s,\chi)=\sum\chi(n)n^{-s}\) initially also requires \(\sigma>1\). [Classical definitions](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.2).

Use the Euler–Maclaurin approximation
\[
\zeta(s)\approx\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}n^{-s}+\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}+\frac12N^{-s}+\sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{B_{2k}}{(2k)!}(s)_{2k-1}N^{1-s-2k},
\]
where \((s)_j=s(s+1)\cdots(s+j-1)\). Choose \(N=64,M=8\); \(B_2,\ldots,B_{16}=1/6,-1/30,1/42,-1/30,5/66,-691/2730,7/6,-3617/510\). Evaluate powers using real logarithms of positive integers. The omitted remainder is controlled; floating-point error dominates here. [Euler–Maclaurin representation](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.2#iii).

The landscape is \(h(\sigma,t)=\log(1+|\zeta(\sigma+it)|)\), over \([0,1.2]\times[12,32]\), excluding the pole automatically. An implementable world embedding is \(G(\sigma,t)=(8(\sigma-.6),.45(t-22),2h-1.6)\). Precompute a 33×97 grid; insert the critical line, frontier coordinates and exact sampled zero ordinates as additional grid nodes. Opening closeups can use the subdomain \([.1,.9]\times[13.3,15]\). Constant-\(t\) and constant-\(\sigma\) curves are restrictions of G. Use interpolation of cached values, never fresh zeta evaluations per frame. Color monotonically by h. This graph is homeomorphic to its rectangular domain, with conical minima near simple zeros; its mesh is neither a physical manifold nor a proof.

For prime ribs, use \((2j,.4t,\log(1+|(1-p^{-1.25-it})^{-1}|))\), with \(p=2,3,5\), \(j=0,1,2\), and \(-4\le t\le4\). They depict individual factor magnitudes in the convergence region. Their transformation into the complex-plane composition is explanatory staging.

Extrude the critical strip using \(B(\sigma,t,v)=(8(\sigma-.6),.45(t-22),v)\), with \(0\le\sigma\le1\), \(12\le t\le32\), and \(-1.6\le v\le2\). Frontier curtains are \(B(a,t,v)\); the gold spine is \(B(1/2,t,-1.6)\). Mark sampled known zeros at \(1/2+it_j\), where
\[
(t_j)=(14.134725141734693,21.022039638771555,25.01085758014569,30.424876125859513).
\]
Keep them fixed. RH places every nontrivial zero on the spine. Quasi-RH asks for some fixed \(\theta<1\) excluding zeros with \(\Re s>\theta\). The manuscript advances \(11/12\to7/8\), moving the right frontier left by \(1/24\). Zeta symmetry \(\rho\mapsto1-\bar\rho\) then confines nontrivial zeros to the closed interval \([1/8,7/8]\). Boundaries remain unresolved. The finite window illustrates an assertion at every height. [Zero symmetry and RH](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.10).

For the topology closeup, let \(\rho=1/2+14.134725141734693i\), \(r=.1\), \(s(\phi)=\rho+re^{i\phi}\), and \(w(\phi)=\zeta(s(\phi))\), \(0\le\phi\le2\pi\). Embed the two complex planes as \(E_j(z)=O_j+k_j(\Re z\,e_j+\Im z\,f_j)\), with orthonormal oriented bases. Display \(E_1(s-\rho)\) and \(E_2(w)\), disclosing their separate magnifications. Precompute 513 paired vertices. Both moving points must share the same segment index and interpolation fraction; independent arc-length motion breaks correspondence.

Numerically, \(\zeta'(\rho)\approx.783296512+.124699830i\). The local approximation is \(\zeta(s)\approx\zeta'(\rho)(s-\rho)\). For an isolated zero of multiplicity m, a sufficiently small positive loop has image winding m; this sampled simple zero illustrates m=1. This is complex-plane winding, not a change in surface genus. [Argument principle](https://math.mit.edu/classes/18.783/2023/LectureSlides15.pdf).

For the reciprocal sculpture, take \(q=ue^{i\phi}\), \(0\le u\le.25\), and lift its local-plane embedding by \(.8\log(1+\min(80,|\zeta(\rho+q)|^{-1}))\) along the plane normal. Assign the capped value at the center; label “reciprocal magnitude capped at 80.” Fixed-\(\phi\) sections expose the spike. Analytically, a zero of order m gives a reciprocal pole of order m; the displayed cap only limits the visualization.

The Eisenstein lattice is \(\mathbb Z[\tau]\), \(\tau=(-1+i\sqrt3)/2\). Vertices are \((m-n/2,\sqrt3n/2,0)\), with norm \(m^2-mn+n^2\). Use integers \(|m|,|n|\le5\), cropped by norm ≤25. Unit edges follow index differences \((1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\); the cell area is \(\sqrt3/2\). An optional norm lift has height \(.08(m^2-mn+n^2)\), explicitly labeled. Hecke characters weight ideals, not these individual lattice points.

The manuscript compares reflection and Poisson representations of completed cubic-theta sums. Reflection supplies a direct bound; Poisson isolates a principal reciprocal-L signal and remaining character rows. Part II changes the normalized sum through prime compensation, unequal scales, inverse second moments and plain-polynomial fourth-moment control. Label this a proof schematic. Ribbons can use \(R_j(u,v)=(4u-2,j+.12v,.35\sin\pi u)\), \(u\in[0,1]\), \(v\in[-1,1]\); their shapes encode no measured character data.

For the conditional climax, define \(\beta_*\) as the supremum of \(\{1/2\}\) and real parts of primitive finite-order Hecke-family zeros in \([1/2,1]\). Exclude poles. Assume \(\Delta_0=\beta_*-\sigma_0>0\). Choose target-independent \(0<\omega<\Delta_0\) and \(\sigma>0\); here σ denotes a saving exponent. Constants may depend on the target η.

Delete finitely many Euler factors: \(L_F^S=L_F\prod_{\mathfrak p\in S}(1-\eta(\mathfrak p)(N\mathfrak p)^{-s})\). These factors cannot vanish for \(\Re s>0\). Require Hη holomorphic with \(\sup_{\Re s>\sigma_0}|H_\eta-1|\le1/2\). For \(Z>0\), the exact signal is
\[
f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Re s=2}Z^{C(s)}e^{(s-5/6)^2}\frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_F^S(s,\eta)}\,ds.
\]
First teach “small sum + small difference ⇒ small signal,” then reveal
\[
|J_\eta|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\sigma_0)+\omega},\quad |J_\eta-f_\eta|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\sigma}.
\]
Since C has slope one, the triangle inequality gives \(|f_\eta|\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\epsilon_*}\), with \(\epsilon_*=\min(\Delta_0-\omega,\sigma)>0\).

Rapid decay as \(Z\downarrow0\) and this infinity bound make \(F_\eta(s)=\int_0^\infty f_\eta(Z)Z^{-C(s)}dZ/Z\) holomorphic for \(\Re s>\beta_*-\epsilon_*\). Fourier inversion and identity identify Fη with the Gaussian-weighted reciprocal initially for \(\Re s>1\). Since \(|H_\eta|\ge1/2\), \(e^{-(s-5/6)^2}F_\eta/H_\eta\) continues the reciprocal holomorphically. The supremum supplies some target zero inside this region, whose reciprocal must have a pole: contradiction. The extension need not reach σ₀. No attained rightmost zero or cancellation of poles is assumed. [Retained manuscript, Proposition 2.1 and Section 20](https://github.com/HarleyCoops/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/build/paper.tex).

Part I uses \(C(s)=s-2/3\), \(C(11/12)=1/4\); Part II uses \(C(s)=s-11/16\), \(C(7/8)=3/16\). A schematic numerical example is \(\beta_*=.9,\omega=.01,\sigma=.008\): ε*=.008, continuation begins at .892, and the two exponents are .1975 and .2045. These are illustrative parameters, not proof data.

The norm lift factors the Hecke function into Dirichlet functions for χ and χχ₋₃, away from harmless finite Euler factors; principal poles require separate treatment. Attribute the strict, uniform \(\Re s>7/8\) conclusion for zeta, every Dirichlet L-function and finite-order Hecke L-functions over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})\) to the manuscript. Nonvanishing supplies no uniform magnitude lower bound. Full RH remains open in the source. End: “OpenAI manuscript / 30 September 2026 / family 003. Full proof and Lean build not independently checked.”
checks: Read retained LaTeX: definitions, Proposition 2.1, Part II normalization, quadratic transfer and Section 20; checked formalization scope.
Executed Euler–Maclaurin N=64/M=8: four zero residuals 4.04e-15, 1.20e-14, 7.51e-15, 1.20e-15. Maximum difference against N=96/M=10 across 3,201 grid points: 9.66e-14.

Independent 72-digit Decimal Euler-transformed eta calculation at nine test points and four loop quadrants: maximum EM discrepancy 1.76e-14; 240 versus 320 terms differed below 3.1e-59. Analytic EM truncation bound on the rectangle: below 4.76e-17, excluding floating-point error.

Computed 512-segment image winding 1.0000000000000002; minimum sampled image magnitude .07612888; maximum phase step .01279 radians. Local linearization discrepancy ≤4.26% on the sampled loop. These are numerical checks, not interval certificates.

Exact rational arithmetic verified both affine powers and the worked saving example. Local Manim/numpy/mpmath unavailable; inspected local renderer restrictions and official tagged CE 0.19 camera/Surface source. No edits, rendering or delegation.
